newsitem.title: UK: Glencore have no complaint with Chinese zinc.
newsitem.headline: Glencore have no complaint with Chinese zinc.

text.p: Private Swiss-based trading and natural resources group Glencore International AG has no claim pending for any Chinese London Metal Exchange (LME) special high grade registered zinc metal, the company said.

Glencore issued a statement in response to recent market talk that the company had complained to the LME about the quality of the Torch brand zinc ingots produced by the Zhuzhou smelter, a subsidiary of China's CNNC.

It said in the statement, "Glencore markets a sizeable volume of Chinese zinc metal on a regular basis. As is common in shipments with zinc metal from any origin, from time to time complaints associated with either the chemical analysis, packing or appearance may occur.

"Recently upon customer request, we instructed an international inspection company to perform analysis on a limited tonnage of special high grade zinc metal stored in Singapore warehouse, prior to its shipment.

"Upon receipt of the results, delivery was made since the metal was found to be in conformity with the contractual specifications. We have no pending claim for any Chinese LME SHG registered zinc metal.
Glencore also said that it had been purchasing Chinese zinc metal for several years, even before it was registered on the LME, and had found it met the standards of the industry.
"In the spirit of mutual co-operation and benefit between Glencore and the CNNC group, Glencore intends to develop their long term trade relationship with CNNC." the statement said.
